1378.summary: The class explores God's hand in the lives of His people during their time in Egypt, focusing on the plagues and the deliverance from slavery. It emphasizes how God's actions were meant to guide His people and give them one heart to follow His commandments.

1379.summary: The class explores the hand of God in our lives through the plagues of Egypt and the role of the serpent, emphasizing God's judgment on sin and the atonement through Jesus Christ. It also discusses the importance of sharing God's work and encouragement with others.

1380.summary: The class explores the role of Moses as a mediator and the significance of the sounding of the trumpet in Exodus, drawing parallels to the work of Jesus Christ. It emphasizes the importance of sanctification, preparation, and covenant relationship with God, culminating in the anticipation of Christ's return.

1381.summary: The class explores how God's hand shapes the faith and character of Jesus, Moses, and Elijah during times of loneliness and suffering, emphasizing the importance of prayer and divine encouragement.

1382.summary: The class examines King Asa's reign, focusing on his early reforms and later struggles, emphasizing the importance of perseverance and faith in times of trouble. It highlights Asa's initial success in purging idolatry and encouraging spiritual growth, followed by his eventual failure to seek God's help in his old age.

1383.summary: The class explores the experiences of Paul and Barnabas during their first missionary journey, emphasizing the guiding hand of God despite challenges and opposition. It highlights the theme of suffering and affliction as part of God's purpose.
